name: Rio Verde
queryAndRequestSummary: Separate English and Portuguese discovery found first-party municipal evidence for Rio Verde 360º. The current Wix viewer was followed to its public app configuration, which identified a Rio Verde territory and parcel layer. Anonymous WFS capabilities and a bounded count=3 GeoJSON request returned native ref_id identities, WGS 84 labels, and full parcel polygons.

attemptedRoutes.outcome: HTTP 200; local SUDERV custodian and Rio Verde 360º public lot service evidenced.

scopeLimits: The sample is limited to three full parcel polygons and properties contain exactly one canonical native identity field, id.
Native source fields, mapping, CRS, and composite-key provenance are documented here and in the city record, not in retained GeoJSON properties.
The bounded request was near the exact WUP point but did not establish an exact-point hit; no map extent miss or exact-point miss was treated as citywide absence.
The public service is urban-lot legislation/cadastral-map evidence; it does not expose or qualify title, owner, address, contact, tax, account, or other unsafe fields.
uncertainty: A real local public lot map/service and anonymous geometry response were verified, but runtime integration remains held pending independent serial review. The packet does not claim legal-title registry completeness or source admission.
